title: Make Array Elements Equal to Zero
summary: Given an integer array nums, select an initial position curr where nums[curr] == 0 and a movement direction (left or right).
statement: Given an integer array nums, select an initial position curr where nums[curr] == 0 and a movement direction (left or right). Repeatedly move in the current direction, decrementing nums[curr] by 1 if it is greater than 0 and reversing direction. A selection is valid if all elements in nums become 0. Return the count of valid initial selections.
constraints: Choose an index currently containing zero and an initial direction.
Move one step repeatedly; on a positive value decrement it, reverse direction, then continue.
A selection is valid when the walk leaves the array after reducing every value to zero; return the number of valid index-direction selections.
hints: For a zero start, only the total positive mass on each side matters.
Equal side sums work in both initial directions.
A difference of one works only when starting toward the heavier side; larger differences cannot recover.
Prefix sums compute the two side totals for every zero in one scan.
editorial: Prefix sums compute the two side totals for every zero in one scan.

tests.explanation: Exactly two start-and-direction selections reduce all values to zero.
No zero has sufficiently balanced sums on its two sides.
